public_rationale: Artificial Analysis tested Gemini 3 Pro at launch. It was the most accurate model on factual questions, but it had an 88% hallucination rate: when it did not know the answer, it usually gave a wrong one instead of saying it was unsure. That rate matched Gemini 2.5 Pro and Flash, and the evaluator said the tendency 'remains unchanged.' Google reported better factual accuracy (72.1% on SimpleQA Verified). That shows improvement, but the problem was still there. The claim that hallucinations and unreliability persist holds.
limitations: The phrase 'same kind of problems that all earlier models have had' is broad; the evidence covers hallucination specifically.
Google's own figures show real improvement in accuracy, even though hallucination remained.

our_interpretation: Plain reading: at launch, Gemini 3 still produced hallucinations (confident false answers) and unreliable outputs at meaningful rates, as earlier LLMs did.
This is not a claim that it had not improved at all; it is a claim that the problems remain.
criteria.support_condition: Launch-time independent evaluations or documented failures show Gemini 3 still hallucinating at substantial rates or behaving unreliably.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Launch-time evaluations show Gemini 3's hallucination rate near zero or clearly solved relative to earlier models.
